design_rationale:
TASK 1 WORKLOG / DOSSIER — fleet_business_servicing (Kestrel Commercial Fleet Lease) — round 2

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 1: {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}. Task 0 holds the termination, mileage, late-charge and refund policies and their tools. Claimed here (disjoint): fleet_ext_trac_shortfall_charge (6 factors, bill_trac_deficiency_eb6903d6, agent) and root fleet_ext_deficiency_arrangement_payment (4 factors, remit_arrangement_payment_506aa8ae, owner=user). The two tasks together cover all six extended policies exactly once.
Route-around (frozen blueprint): fleet signer acts carry no numeric field; the customer's own write is the signer authorising the first payment of a deficiency arrangement, a business payment the charter's fleet_payment event records.

1. Why this is a good test. Megan Zielinski (authorized signer, Yardline Grounds Management LLC) asks only for a payment arrangement on what the business owes for TRAC pickup 537, sold at auction on 2026-10-21, with the first payment today. The arrangement rule fixes the first payment only after the unit's ledger carries the deficiency charge billed for its sale settlement; the settlement posted 2026-10-27 records trac_result deficiency but no deficiency charge is billed and charges due are 0.00. The agent must read that sentence, check the ledger, find the deficiency policy that books the charge, compute it (settlement figures, the sale date against the turn-in date, the unit's 12-month late-charge history, the business's retail and balloon contracts and the balloon funding dates), bill it, then compute the first arrangement payment (dates, the deficiency charges, the active balloon contract and the retail late-charge history) and hand it to the signer.

2. Problem-tree card. One edge, value_input on pa_balance, state form, affirmative: "The first arrangement payment is fixed only after the unit's ledger carries the deficiency charge billed for its sale settlement." It passes the four-point test (ordering connective "only after"; a ledger state; no tool, id or code token; a hard requirement scoped to the unit's own settlement). Exactly one write of the difficulty books a fleet_trac_deficiency_charge. Opening falsity: settlement 6e4766b1-e176-4d52-9181-7c3bf360f2f1 trac_result=deficiency, no deficiency posting, charges_due_balance 0.0. Order: deficiency, then arrangement payment. Edge sensitivity: skipping the charge gives a first payment of 0.00.

3. Base-invariant card. Deficiency: fleet_trac_settlement governs; its only gate settle_status applies to fleet_sale_settlement (posted) -> policy_scope. Its overwrites retire the net-proceeds sentence and "when they fall short the shortfall is billed as a deficiency" for short TRAC settlements only, restating the base net proceeds for surplus, even and closed-end settlements, to which its figure does not apply. Arrangement payment: fleet_billing_and_payments gate pay_status (status sold allowed; bound to fleet_unit_id); ACH debit accepted; frozen 2026-11-12 10:20 EST (09:20 CT, a Thursday) is before the 17:00 CT cutoff. Its overwrites retire "due trac_deficiency_payment_days calendar days after the settlement invoice" for arranged deficiencies (restating the base due date otherwise) and the oldest-unpaid-month posting sentence for arrangement payments only (an arrangement payment is booked against the unit's charges due and recorded against no rental month; other payments restated); the tool writes the payment with no billing period, matching that rule.

4. Business-object card. The retail late charges are priced by the published New Vehicle Retail unpaid-installment rule: starting rate 3.5 percent (30 or more installments satisfied, no returned payment) less 0.5 points (clean schedule) = 3.0 percent of the 815.70 unpaid installment = 24.47. The 2026-04-08 and 2026-10-09 charges fall 1 day beyond grace, so they are halved and rounded down to 12.00. The 2026-11-08 charge falls 41 days after the next due date 2026-09-28 and stays at 24.47. The April charge was paid, leaving fees due of 36.47. Fleet reads only their count and dates. Signer requests on the pickup: the completed delivery acceptance of 2024-03-01 and the completed termination notice of 2026-07-02 (the notice date the unit records), as the base acceptance and termination clauses require. The closed 2019 balloon carries its maturity election (pay_balloon), wire payoff of 2022-04-08 and electronic lien release of 2022-04-11, the day it closed. Target fleet unit 15b99b8c-3194-4880-977c-002367e38715 (pickup 537, MLA-517330, SCH-517330-03). Settlement row 6e4766b1-e176-4d52-9181-7c3bf360f2f1: book value retired 20,800.00 (52,000.00 less 30 x 1,040.00), gross 17,900.00, expenses 1,610.00, posted 2026-10-27 for the 2026-10-21 sale. All rentals 2024-03..2026-08 are paid; the 2025-09 and 2026-04 rentals were paid late and their 25.00 late charges (2025-10-07, 2026-05-07) are paid. The arranged balance is the unit's charges_due_balance, raised by the deficiency tool and lowered by the payment tool.

5. Factor cards (tier / evidence / baseline figure):
 Deficiency 3,907.90 (whole baseline 4,860.00): d_relationship_remarketing 150, active retail and balloon (4,097.90); d_sale_expense_allowance method, sale 58 days after turn-in -> min(1,610, 8 percent of 17,900) (4,077.00); d_term_completion_relief 5 percent, 29 of 42 months (4,132.00); d_notice_lead_credit 200, 53 days (4,107.90); d_payment_history_credit 50, one late charge in 12 months (3,957.90); d_balloon_tenure_credit 100, balloon funded 36 or more months ago (4,007.90).
 Arrangement payment 1,257.31 (baseline 3,907.90 = pay in full): pa_term_months_rule method, 9 months to scheduled end (3,907.90); pa_down_share_schedule 10 percent (3,907.90); pa_minimum_down_schedule 500 (1,172.37); pa_upfront_count_schedule 2, two retail late charges in 6 months (878.66).
 Near-miss records in the seed: the settlement posting date 2026-10-27 (64 days after turn-in -> actual expenses) vs the sale date 2026-10-21 (58 days -> the 8 percent cap); the closed 2019 balloon contract (not active, so it does not count toward the remarketing tier or the arrangement-months rule); the fleet late charge of 2025-10-07 (13 whole months back) outside the 12-month history; the retail late charge of 2026-04-08 (7 whole months back) outside the 6-month window.
 Factor independence (transitive): each factor reads only F/P/K, DAYS/MONTHS, LATEST/SUM/COUNT on this unit, EXISTS on retail/balloon, XCOUNT over the retail and balloon ledgers, and plain bindings (d_book_retired, d_gross, d_expenses_actual, pa_balance); assembly only in result.
 Method tiers: sale expenses 5 percent cap / 8 percent cap / actual -> 895.00 / 1,432.00 / 1,610.00 on this sale; arrangement months to scheduled end / fixed 3 / 1 -> 9 / 3 / 1 here.

6. Probes. Absent records: no balloon -> remarketing one-contract tier, no tenure credit, fixed 3 months; no retail late charges with an active retail -> nothing up front; no notice -> no notice credit (guarded); no deficiency charge -> minimum down payment nothing and a zero arranged balance. Other-holding reads are EXISTS with exact filters or XCOUNT over the whole ledger, so no first-match ambiguity remains.

7. Persona. Megan volunteers the turn-in in late August, the auction sale on October 21st and the arrangement ask (all in the seed); identity details, unit, signer status and other accounts (including the paid-off 2019 balloon) only when asked; she authorises posting whatever must come first only when told, chooses an ACH debit, authorises exactly the stated first payment and ends when told it posted.

8. Standard solution. find_customers(name) -> verify (phone, EIN4, ZIP) -> find_fleet_units -> find_fleet_transactions -> find_fleet_requests -> find_retail_contracts -> find_retail_transactions -> find_balloon_contracts -> find_balloon_transactions -> bill deficiency 3,907.90 -> hand over -> signer authorises 1,257.31 by ach_debit. check_compute recomputes both values at handling time.
user_scenario:
You are Megan Zielinski, the controller of Yardline Grounds Management LLC, a landscaping and snow-removal company in Plymouth, Michigan, and the authorized signer named on its Kestrel fleet master lease. You are calm, methodical and a little tired of surprises this quarter, and you like to hear a figure before you commit to it. You open by explaining that your company turned in pickup 537 in late August, that it sold at auction on October 21st, and that from the auction paperwork you understand it brought less than its book value, so Yardline will owe Kestrel the difference. Cash is tight going into the snow season, so you cannot pay that whole difference at once: you want to set up whatever payment arrangement Kestrel offers on it and make the first payment today, while you are on the phone. You have no figure in mind for the difference or for the first payment and you rely on the representative to work them out from Kestrel's records.
Only when asked how to find the account do you give the business's legal name, Yardline Grounds Management LLC. To confirm identity you give, as asked, the business phone 3135550389, the last four of the company's EIN, 5617, and the billing ZIP code 48170; if one more detail is wanted, the account email is accounts@yardlinegrounds.com. If asked which unit, you say pickup 537 under master lease agreement MLA-517330; you do not have the VIN to hand. If asked, you confirm you are the authorized signer on the master agreement. If the representative asks about other Kestrel accounts, you say the company finances a pickup on a Kestrel retail contract and a sedan on a balloon contract, that an older balloon contract on a previous sedan was paid off a few years ago, and that you have not looked at those accounts this month; you do not have their account numbers with you.
If the representative tells you that something has to be put on the pickup's account before the arrangement can be worked out, you tell them to go ahead. When the representative asks how the first payment should be made, you say Kestrel should debit the company's operating account on file by ACH. When the representative tells you the first payment amount and hands the payment over for you to authorize as the signer, you authorize it for pickup 537 with exactly that amount as an ACH debit. If the figure the representative gives is more than you hoped, you say so once, briefly, and still go ahead. Once you are told the payment has posted, you thank the representative, say you will watch for the arrangement statement, and end the call.

edges.condition: For a TRAC unit whose sale settlement shows trac_result deficiency, the unit's ledger carries a fleet_trac_deficiency_charge posting and the unit's charges due balance includes it.
edges.policy_source: The first arrangement payment is fixed only after the unit's ledger carries the deficiency charge billed for its sale settlement.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The settlement of 2026-10-27 records trac_result deficiency, yet no posting on the pickup is a fleet_trac_deficiency_charge and its charges due balance is 0.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite edge: the deficiency charge must land before the first arrangement payment is figured, as the arrangement rule's prerequisite sentence states; nothing parallel to reorder.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the deficiency charge leaves the arranged balance and the minimum down payment at nothing and the first arrangement payment at 0.00 instead of 1,257.31; the ledger lacks the 3,907.90 charge.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona says only that the sold pickup brought less than its book value and that she wants a payment arrangement with a first payment today; she never says a charge is missing or must be billed first; her only related line is passive ('If the representative tells you that something has to be put on the pickup's account ... you tell them to go ahead').
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: remit_arrangement_payment_506aa8ae looks up the unit only to read its customer id and balance and then books the payment; it never checks for a deficiency charge and returns a normal receipt. bill_trac_deficiency_eb6903d6 likewise posts without any check beyond the unit's existence.
